lateral.Position: Real Estate Investment and Finance Associate
lateral.Offices: Charlotte, North Carolina; New York, New York
lateral.Job Description: Katten, a global Am Law 100 firm, is seeking an associate to join its premier Real Estate Investment and Finance group in the Charlotte or New York office. Qualified candidates will have 2-4 years of complex commercial real estate experience at a nationally or regionally recognized law firm and be admitted to the North Carolina or New York State Bar or eligible for submission on waiver. Required experience should include experience with real estate debt and equity transactions, drafting transactional documents, including loan documents, experience with transactional due diligence review, including title and survey matters, and the ability to manage all aspects of transactional closings. Our ideal candidate will thrive in a fast-paced environment, demonstrate sound judgment, and take ownership of work assignment responsibilities. The estimated salary range for this role is $235,000 - $365,000. Salary determinations are made based on numerous factors, such as, but not limited to experience/job history and class/graduation year.

Farella Braun + Martel’s leading intellectual property litigation practice is seeking a talented and motivated Patent Litigation Associate to join our distinguished IP team. The ideal candidate will have 2-5 years of experience in patent litigation, with a strong understanding of patent law and litigation procedures, excellent legal research, writing, and analytical skills, strong communication and interpersonal skills. A degree in engineering, computer science, or a related technical field is strongly preferred but not required. Our IP litigators engage in high-stakes patent litigation involving diverse industries spanning computer hardware and software, telecommunications, and e-commerce to solar and wind power technologies. Our clients range from Fortune 100 corporations to emerging start-ups, all of whom trust us to handle their most significant IP disputes with agility and precision. The annual base compensation range for this California position is between $222,500 and $290,000. Placement within the salary range depends upon a number of factors including but not limited to years of relevant experience and professional skills required for this role. Additional compensation may include discretionary hours-based and additional bonuses, health/welfare benefits, vacation and leave time (including parental and sabbatical) and paid holidays.

lateral.Position: Chicago – Litigation – Mid to Senior Level – Associate
lateral.Job Description: Skadden’s Litigation team in the Chicago office is seeking outstanding lateral candidates (Class of 2020 – 2022) with litigation experience, including discovery, brief writing, and pre-trial preparation activity. Exposure and interest in the cybersecurity and data privacy practice is a plus. The ideal candidate has significant experience handling complex litigation and white collar matters, including securities litigation; class actions and MDLs; cyber litigation; commercial contractual disputes; fraud, breach of fiduciary duty and tortious interference claims; merger-related litigation and control disputes; bankruptcy and restructuring-related issues; and regulatory investigation. High level of academic achievement and experience in the Litigation practice of a peer firm are preferred qualifications. Qualified candidates should be admitted to practice law in Illinois. The starting base salary for this position is expected to be between $310,000 to $390,000 annually. Actual salary will be determined based on skills, experience (to the extent relevant) and other job-related factors, consistent with applicable law. This position may be eligible for a discretionary year-end bonus. Associates who join Skadden laterally participate in an enhanced mentor program, which specifically focuses on the unique needs experienced attorneys face during professional transitions. These efforts, along with our professional development and other Skadden benefits , including a hybrid work model*, offer a dynamic environment where all can shape their own career trajectories while contributing to groundbreaking legal work. We also have an extensive pro bono program that allows attorneys to devote, and receive credit for, time for myriad causes that spark their interests and matches those interests with the legal needs in the community. *Our current hybrid work model consists of working Monday through Thursday in the office. Attorneys also receive the opportunity to work remotely for specified periods throughout the year. EEO Statement Skadden is an Equal Opportunity Employer. It does not discriminate against applicants or employees based on any legally impermissible factor including, but not limited to, race, color, religion, creed, sex, national origin, ancestry, age, alienage or citizenship status, marital or familial status, domestic partnership status, caregiver status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, change of sex or transgender status, genetic information, medical condition, pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions, sexual and reproductive health decisions, disability, any protected military or veteran status, or status as a victim of domestic or dating violence, sexual assault or offense, or stalking. Applicants who require an accommodation during the application process should contact Alex Taylor at (212) 735-2176. Hanson Bridgett's Los Angeles office is growing, and we're looking for an associate with 2–5 years of experience in public agency and/or environmental law — especially water — to join a statewide team with a practice as dynamic as California itself. You'll work directly with a partner on a mix of transactions, advice & counsel, and/or litigation spanning water rights, Clean Water Act, CEQA, Brown Act, eminent domain, public finance, infrastructure, government procurement, construction and prevailing wage, real estate, legislative drafting, and the Government Claims Act. Prior experience at a government agency or in communications is a bonus. We are looking for an ambitious team player with a positive, can-do attitude. Humility and a sense of humor required. While we offer the ability to work remotely in an agile (hybrid) manner, this position will be expected to work alongside senior attorneys in Hanson Bridgett’s Los Angeles office approximately 3-4 days a week. The annual base compensation range for this California position is approximately $195,000 to $245,000 depending on experience. Placement within the salary range depends upon a number of factors including, but not limited to years of experience and professional skills required for this role. At Hanson Bridgett, you’ll have close, supportive relationships with your peers and partners — getting exposure to clients early and taking on challenging projects with our existing team. When you work here, you’ll get: Immediate client exposure on meaningful projects Professional mentorship opportunities, with peers and partners to help shape your career and grow your own book of business A values-based, B Corp firm with forward-thinking policies, A work environment that supports your growth Ideal candidates will have a distinguished academic background and impeccable references. CA Bar required. Strong research, writing and communication skills, high level of analytical skills as well as excellent and highly adaptable communication skills are required. We seek intelligent, entrepreneurial, team players who are practical, problem solvers, ambitious, organized, and detail oriented and are looking towards a partnership with Hanson Bridgett. We are an EEO employer and offer a competitive salary and benefits package. To be considered for a position, please submit: Cover letter (optional) Resume Law school transcript Writing sample or Deal Sheet

lateral.Offices: New York, New York; Washington, D.C.
lateral.Job Description: Eversheds Sutherland (US) LLP is seeking an Associate to join its Insurance Products Group, a premier regulatory practice, to work on sophisticated matters at the intersection of insurance and securities regulation. This position is open in our New York or Washington, D.C. offices. Eversheds Sutherland’s Insurance Products Group has decades of experience advising life insurance companies on the complex laws and business relationships involved in the development, registration, administration, and distribution of life and retirement products. It is the nation’s leading practice on the regulation of insurance contracts by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission ( e.g. , variable and index-linked annuities and life insurance policies). Associates in the Insurance Products Group work closely with Partners who are widely recognized for their expertise in insurance and securities regulation. The position offers direct mentorship, hands‑on experience, and the opportunity to develop deep, market leading expertise in insurance and securities regulation. Key experience, skills, and responsibilities: Experience: 2-5 years of regulatory compliance experience (law firm, regulator, or in-house) focused on (a) the U.S. federal securities laws ( i.e. , the Investment Company Act of 1940, Securities Act of 1933, or Securities Exchange Act of 1934) and/or (b) insurance regulation Demonstrated ability to navigate complex regulatory frameworks Commitment to building expertise in a specialized area of law and immersion into the insurance industry Effective project and time management skills Collaboration with cross-functional teams Direct engagement with clients, regulators, and industry associations The Insurance Products Group is part of Eversheds Sutherland’s broader Insurance group, which is ranked as “Band 2” with Chambers USA. Eversheds Sutherland hires individuals who will contribute to our culture and reputation for excellence. Our dedication to providing unparalleled client service means that we are seeking talented candidates who will grow and thrive within our firm. We recruit individuals with impressive credentials and direct or translatable work experience, focusing on candidates who reflect the Firm’s core values, including self-motivation, professionalism, and creativity. Overall, we seek candidates whose personal qualities, skills, engagement level and interests will enhance and enrich the Firm. We provide our employees with: Interesting work with industry-leading practices and an impressive client list. Significant practical training, informal training, and formal training programs. An approachable and supportive culture. We are guided by our five core values of collaboration, inclusivity, openness, creativity, and professionalism in all that we do as a Firm. A commitment to programs that identify ways to create and maintain a culture that reflects our values when it comes to inclusion, representation, and opportunity. We appreciate the significant role diverse perspectives play in our service to clients and our development. Thorough benefits options and thoughtful wellness programs. We invite any qualified candidate who would like to become a valued contributor to an established and talented team of attorneys to “Apply Now” with your resume, transcripts, and writing sample. The Associate position requires in-office presence three days per week. The salary is commensurate with years of relevant experience & geographic location. The salary range for our Associate position is $235,000-365,000. The New York office of Loeb & Loeb’s market-leading Art Law group is seeking a highly motivated associate with 6–7 years of experience to join our dynamic team. This is a unique opportunity for a transaction-driven attorney—ideally with a corporate background—who thrives on complex, high-value deal work and is eager to apply their skills in the fast-evolving global art market. We represent a prestigious roster of clients, including ultra-high-net-worth collectors, top-tier galleries, and art-backed lenders, in sophisticated transactions often exceeding $100M. The work is technically challenging and rarely routine spanning the unique facets of the global art industry. Key Responsibilities: Draft, review, negotiate, and manage a wide range of transactional documents, including sale agreements, consignment agreements, auction agreements, loan agreements, deeds of gift, etc. Provide nuanced legal analysis across intersecting areas such as tax, intellectual property, cultural property, customs, endangered species regulations, and AML/KYC compliance. Ideal Candidate: JD required Admitted to the New York State Bar (active and in good standing) 6–7 years of experience at a reputable law firm, with a focus on corporate or transactional law Exceptional drafting, analytical, and organizational skills—with speed and precision under tight deadlines A genuine passion for deal-making and a curiosity about the art world (prior art law experience is a plus, but not required) Proven ability to manage multiple high-stakes matters simultaneously in a fast-paced environment Team-oriented, with strong communication skills and a collaborative spirit This role offers significant growth potential and direct mentorship from leading practitioners. While the practice demands excellence, it maintains a strong team culture. If you love transactions, thrive on complexity, and are looking for a fresh, intellectually rich challenge in a globally recognized practice, we’d love to hear from you. This position’s in-office requirement is 5 days per week, and after six months of employment, associates may work remotely on Fridays. The expected salary range for this position is $285,000.00 – $325,000.00 annually (commensurate with experience). This range could fluctuate based on varying factors. Interested candidates should submit their resume, law school transcript, and a cover letter explaining your interest in the role.

lateral.Position: Finance Associate Attorney – Leveraged Finance (4th–5th Year)
lateral.Offices: Chicago, Illinois; New York, New York; Washington, D.C.
lateral.Job Description: Sheppard is seeking a 4th–5th year associate to join our nationally recognized Leveraged Finance and Private Equity Finance team within the Finance Practice Group. This position is open to candidates in New York, Washington, D.C., or Chicago. Exceptional candidates may be considered for other firm locations. Sheppard, Mullin, Richter & Hampton LLP is a global Am Law 50 full-service law firm with over 1,200 attorneys across 16 offices worldwide, advising clients on high-stakes litigation, complex transactions, and cutting-edge regulatory matters across key industries—including energy, real estate and development, financial services, healthcare, and technology. Sheppard is known for its collaborative culture. Our Leveraged Finance and Private Equity Finance team represents private equity sponsors, their portfolio companies, corporate borrowers, and debt providers in a broad range of financing transactions. We advise clients throughout the private equity investment lifecycle, including acquisition financings, growth financings, dividend recapitalizations, refinancings, and exits. Our team is known for efficient execution, deep market knowledge, and practical, business-oriented counsel. The ideal candidate will have experience with: Representing private equity sponsors and their portfolio companies in connection with borrower-side debt financing transactions, including acquisition financings and dividend recapitalizations. Exposure to deal terms, documentation conventions and industry practices related to acquisition financing across market segments, including bilateral deals, club deals, bank loans, direct lending and broadly syndicated loans. Drafting, negotiating, and structuring definitive loan documents, including commitment letters, credit agreements, intercreditor agreements, seller notes, legal opinions, guaranty and security documents, and other ancillary debt financing documentation. Independently managing transaction workstreams, coordinating closings, and serving as a day-to-day contact for clients and deal teams across multiple financing transactions. Collaborating with Corporate/M&A and other practice groups on acquisition financing transactions, including M&A diligence and negotiations related to the financing provisions of purchase agreements. Candidates with experience primarily representing lenders are encouraged to apply, particularly those interested in developing a sponsor-focused practice. Qualifications: Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited law school 4–5 years of relevant leveraged finance or acquisition finance experience Strong academic credentials and excellent drafting, negotiation, analytical, and written communication skills Resume, cover letter, and law school transcript are required to apply. Candidates must be admitted to and a member in good standing of the bar in the jurisdiction of the office to which they apply. The annual salary range for this position is $310,000-$365,000. Contact: For inquiries, please reach out to Katherine Milanes at kmilanes@sheppard.com . Req #: 2026-26101

Qualifications: Greenberg Glusker is seeking a junior corporate associate (1–3 years of experience) to join its nationally recognized Corporate Group. Salary range: $210,000 – $230,000 per year For specific inquiries, please contact recruiting@greenbergglusker.com . Why Work Here Health, Wellness & Work-Life Balance We believe exceptional work begins with supporting the people behind it. That's why Greenberg Glusker invests in programs and benefits designed to promote the health, well-being, and work-life balance of our team members: Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and their eligible dependents, as well as life insurance, short- and long-term disability coverage, and accidental death and dismemberment insurance. Employees can also start a Health Savings Account (HSA) or Flexible Spending Account (FSA) to help save for healthcare costs. All full-time team members receive free, unlimited access to a confidential Employee Assistance Program, offering 24/7 counseling services, financial resources, legal consultations, and other wellness support. Beyond traditional benefits, we encourage healthy living through access to an on-site fitness center as well as our through our wellness webinars and challenges. We also provide paid time off and generous paid parental leave. Just as importantly, we foster a culture where attorneys are expected to respect one another's time, recognizing that personal well-being is essential to long-term professional success. Professional Development & Mentorship At Greenberg Glusker, we believe exceptional attorneys are developed through meaningful experience, thoughtful mentorship, and opportunities to build successful, long-term careers. This looks like: Early Responsibility & Meaningful Experience – Greenberg Glusker offers the best of both worlds: the sophistication of a leading law firm with the opportunities for early exposure that come with being a mid-sized practice. Our size allows associates to work directly with clients earlier, take on sophisticated legal work, and develop meaningful responsibility that serve as the foundation for a thriving career. A Dual-Mentor Program – Every new associate is paired with both a senior associate and a partner mentor. Senior associates – or “Big Sibs” – serve as day-to-day resources, providing practical guidance as associates navigate life at the Firm. In addition, each associate is matched with a partner-level mentor who offers broader career guidance, helping to chart a path for professional growth and long-term success. Hands-On Professional Development – We are committed to the continuous education and advancement of our attorneys. Through our Associate Training Program, attorneys engage in learning opportunities designed to strengthen legal, business, and practice-specific skills while receiving ongoing mentorship from experienced practitioners. A Voice in the Firm – Associates at Greenberg Glusker are encouraged to play an active role in the Firm's direction. Many serve on Firm committees where their ideas and perspectives are genuinely valued. Business Development Support – Building a successful legal career extends beyond practicing law. Associates have access to the Firm's marketing, public relations, and business development resources and are encouraged to attend events and conferences to develop relationships that fuel future practice growth. Diversity & Inclusion Founded in 1959 by lawyers who were not welcome in traditional law firms due to religious discrimination, our firm has always valued skill, dedication, and integrity above all else. That legacy continues to shape our commitment to excellence and inclusion in the legal profession, guiding how we recruit, retain, and advance talent at every level. We are intentional about fostering a supportive culture and inclusive workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging and has an equal opportunity to succeed. That same commitment extends beyond our walls, as we engage with the broader community through pro bono work, public interest partnerships, and initiatives aimed at promoting social justice and expanding access to the legal profession. Recent initiatives include: Pro bono partnerships benefiting low-income, underserved communities, with unlimited billable credit for associates Volunteer efforts and fundraising for a variety of causes that matter to the communities where we live and work Book scholarships for first-year law students in Southern California Longstanding participation in the Association of Corporate Counsel SoCal Summer Internship Program Leadership roles held by our attorneys in various legal and business organizations Support for mission-driven organizations and local businesses Internal and external programming, including educational events and community-building activities Giving Back Community involvement is an important part of Greenberg Glusker's culture. We believe giving back strengthens not only the communities we serve, but also the connections within our own Firm. In addition to our commitment to pro bono service, our team regularly participates in volunteer initiatives and charitable fundraising throughout the year. Recent examples include: Law Rocks Fundraiser – Greenberg Glusker’s in-house band, The Gee Gees, have participated three years in a row in the annual Law Rocks Los Angeles competition. The band has won the Judge’s Choice Award and has raised tens of thousands of dollars for local charities like Alliance for Children’s Rights and TreePeople. Starve-A-Vampire Blood Drive – In partnership with the American Red Cross, team members participate in our annual October blood drive, complete with festive decorations, refreshments, and music. Last year alone, 30 participants helped support up to 90 lives. Food From The Bar – Through creative fundraising events – including Pie-a-Partner, lip sync competitions, karaoke, casino nights, comedy shows, and magic shows – we have raised thousands of dollars for the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank. Adopt-A-Family – Every holiday season, our team comes together to provide gifts and support for families in need. Volunteer Service – From building homes with Habitat for Humanity to preparing meals at Our Big Kitchen Los Angeles, our team enjoys opportunities to serve the community together. A Culture of Appreciation At Greenberg Glusker, we profoundly subscribe to the belief that our workforce is our most valuable asset, and we pair that belief with action to ensure that our team members feel valued: Administrative Professionals Day – Each year, we recognize Administrative Professionals Day with a week of appreciation events, which have included firm-sponsored massages, catered treats, gifts, and attorneys serving breakfast to our staff. Personal & Professional Milestones – Throughout the year, we celebrate birthdays, work anniversaries, engagements, weddings, growing families, retirements, and other personal milestones through our firm newsletter and office celebrations. Years of Service Recognition – At our annual holiday party, team members receive a Greenberg Glusker lapel pin upon reaching five years with the Firm, and for every five years thereafter, a diamond is added to the pin – a meaningful tradition to honor long-term dedication and commitment. Building Community Beyond the Office Greenberg Glusker creates opportunities throughout the year for colleagues to connect outside of client work. Beyond the design of our Century City office, which features open kitchens and collaborative gathering spaces that encourage conversation, teamwork, and spontaneous connection throughout the day, examples include: Attorney Retreats & Ski Trips – Each year, our attorneys enjoy a weekend retreat in Ojai, California, as well as an annual ski trip, providing opportunities to build relationships, recharge, and connect outside the office. July 4th Family Breakfast – An annual summertime tradition where team members and their families gather for breakfast, face painting, balloon artists, crafts, and other family-friendly activities. Private Movie Screenings – Whether celebrating the release of a highly anticipated film or one our attorneys helped bring to life, we host private screenings at the AMC Century City theater, often inviting team members to bring a guest. Halloween Celebration & Office Trick-or-Treating – One of our most anticipated annual traditions, Halloween at Greenberg Glusker features festive decorations, themed lunches, costume contests, and office-wide trick-or-treating for employees' children, with candy stations hosted across all three floors. Thanksgiving Potluck – Before the holiday, team members gather to share homemade dishes while the Firm provides turkey and other favorites. Those who prefer not to cook can instead support the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank through a charitable donation, making the event a celebration of both community and giving. And Much More – Throughout the year, you'll also find escape rooms, happy hours, Office Olympics, cocktail-making classes, office mini golf, and other opportunities to relax, celebrate, and enjoy time together.

lateral.Job Description: Holland & Hart is seeking a mid-level associate to join our nationally ranked Energy, Environment and Natural Resources practice. The application window is anticipated to close on or after September 30, 2026. Holland & Hart reserves the right to close the position prior to or after this date. Based in Nevada—one of the world’s premier mining jurisdictions—our team sits at the center of the domestic critical minerals and energy boom. We secure landmark results on cutting edge bet the company litigation for clients developing vital projects on public lands, navigating complex regulatory hurdles at a time when domestic mineral production is crucial to the nation’s security and energy future. As an associate on our team, you will collaborate directly with Chambers-ranked partners, engage face-to-face with federal and state agencies, and build elite expertise in a high-stakes, fast-moving legal sector. Ready to shape the future of critical mineral energy law? Position Requirements Ideal candidates will have three to seven years of environmental law experience or a background in general litigation matters with an interest in mining and water rights and openness for training. Administrative litigation and regulatory experience are a plus. This position involves water rights, permitting review, and defending litigation on federal and state permits. We are seeking candidates who are excited to be part of a dynamic team, ready to take ownership of matters (with appropriate supervision, mentorship, and guidance) and eager to get to know our clients. Candidates should demonstrate a teamwork ethic, critical analytical skills, strong written and verbal communication skills, and the ability to excel under pressure and thrive under demanding schedules and deadlines. Practical law school experience (law review, law journal, moot court, or trial advocacy team), and/or judicial clerkship experience are highly desired. Compensation and Expectations Holland & Hart’s compensation is merit-based—you’ll be evaluated on your individual performance and achievements. In compliance with applicable state and local pay transparency laws, the anticipated salary range for this role is $215,000 – $270,000 for applicants based in Colorado, and is $180,000 – $205,000 for applicants based in Nevada. Our generous bonus program rewards financial contributions and hard work and associates are also eligible for fee splits. Holland & Hart expects associates to invest 1800 hours on billable matters, 75 hours of pro bono/public service work (or 50 hours of pro bono legal work), in addition to at least 25 hours dedicated to Community-building, Diversity & Inclusion Investment hours. Contributions to the life of the firm is vital to the collective success of the firm, and we encourage our lawyers to engage in ways each person finds meaningful through various committees and firm activities. Benefits Summary Holland & Hart promotes work/life balance with a robust wellness program, unlimited PTO, a reduced time program, and a sabbatical program for eligible employees and partners. Full-time employees become eligible for benefits on the date of hire, with a benefits offering that includes medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, EAP, STD, and LTD. Additionally the firm provides enhanced parental leave for both primary and non-primary caregivers as well as an automatic Off Ramp/On Ramp program before and after parental leave. The firm offers inclusive fertility and family-forming benefits. Also available are voluntary income protection benefits such as supplemental life, accident, critical illness, and hospital indemnity insurances, as well as a 401(k)-retirement plan with a company match. In addition, the firm has programs that may provide for educational assistance, a subscription service for continuing legal education programs, free or discounted legal services, and opportunities through the Holland & Hart Foundation, which is a non-profit organization dedicated to creating volunteer opportunities for lawyers, staff, families, and friends of Holland & Hart LLP. Part-time employees may have access to some of these benefits, which may be on a pro-rated basis. You may address your cover letter and/or direct application questions to Anna Bartle, Recruiting Coordinator, AJBartle@hollandhart.com . Search firm inquiries may be directed to Tia Baker TBBaker@hollandhart.com . No phone calls please. About Holland & Hart Holland & Hart is known for fostering an intentional culture that prioritizes integrity and a passion for ongoing learning and collaboration. We offer sophisticated, challenging projects and diverse, innovating clients. Holland & Hart is ranked as one of Vault’s “Best Law Firms in the Mountain States.” Our core values—integrity, excellence, innovation, teamwork, our commitment to one another, our diverse workforce, our communities, and living full lives—influence all aspects of Holland & Hart’s culture. Holland & Hart attracts those who love what they do at work as much as they love what they do on the weekend. We intentionally create opportunities for attorneys to seek balance in work and in life through longstanding programs including sabbaticals, service opportunities through the Holland & Hart Foundation, team retreats, and flexible-hour, remote, and hybrid work arrangements so they can be in the moment at their job, with their families, or when pursuing personal interests. Holland & Hart is a full-service law firm with more than 500 lawyers in 14 offices. Throughout the Mountain West, from coast to coast and beyond, Holland & Hart provides clients with astute legal counsel from a vantage like no other. For more information, visit hollandhart.com. Holland & Hart is an equal opportunity employer. lateral.Position: Lateral Associate - Corporate: Restructuring & Special Situations (New York)
lateral.Job Description: Sullivan & Cromwell is seeking experienced associates to join the Firm's General Practice (corporate) - Restructuring & Special Situations group. Ideal candidates should have at least three years of experience working in the corporate practice at a law firm with a significant restructuring practice (chapter 11 company side representations, chapter 11 secured creditor representations, out of court restructuring transactions, and/or capital solutions/liability management transactions), as well as significant drafting experience in court motion practice and/or credit documentation. This is an opportunity for experienced lawyers, and as such, current law students are not eligible for consideration. About the Restructuring & Special Situations Group: Sullivan & Cromwell’s award-winning Restructuring & Special Situations Practice is pound-for-pound the most successful practice of its type. With six restructuring partners in New York and four internationally, we have had the honor of successfully resolving many of the most complex global chapter 11 cases ever filed (typically at a fraction of the cost expected) and representing investors in the most profitable strategic and loan-to-own acquisitions implemented in chapter 11. The secret to this success is the integration of the Restructuring practice with the rest of S&C and the Firm’s unique ability to bring “first chair” transactional, litigation and regulatory talent to bear in a distressed environment. Restructuring is the ultimate team sport for lawyers. And no other law firm can mobilize a team like Sullivan & Cromwell because no other law firm has the same combination of talent and trust. S&C’s famous transactional and litigation practices contain many of the leading names of their generations. More importantly, S&C’s celebrated internal culture means that all S&C lawyers are available to assist on every matter as if it were their own. Why Work Here Health, Wellness & Work-Life Balance We believe exceptional work begins with supporting the people behind it. Professional Development & Mentorship At Greenberg Glusker, we believe exceptional attorneys are developed through meaningful experience, thoughtful mentorship, and opportunities to build successful, long-term careers. This looks like: Early Responsibility & Meaningful Experience – Greenberg Glusker offers the best of both worlds: the sophistication of a leading law firm with the opportunities for early exposure that come with being a mid-sized practice. A Dual-Mentor Program – Every new associate is paired with both a senior associate and a partner mentor. Senior associates – or “Big Sibs” – serve as day-to-day resources, providing practical guidance as associates navigate life at the Firm. In addition, each associate is matched with a partner-level mentor who offers broader career guidance, helping to chart a path for professional growth and long-term success. Hands-On Professional Development – We are committed to the continuous education and advancement of our attorneys. Through our Associate Training Program, attorneys engage in learning opportunities designed to strengthen legal, business, and practice-specific skills while receiving ongoing mentorship from experienced practitioners. A Voice in the Firm – Associates at Greenberg Glusker are encouraged to play an active role in the Firm's direction. Many serve on Firm committees where their ideas and perspectives are genuinely valued. Business Development Support – Building a successful legal career extends beyond practicing law. Associates have access to the Firm's marketing, public relations, and business development resources and are encouraged to attend events and conferences to develop relationships that fuel future practice growth. Diversity & Inclusion Founded in 1959 by lawyers who were not welcome in traditional law firms due to religious discrimination, our firm has always valued skill, dedication, and integrity above all else. That legacy continues to shape our commitment to excellence and inclusion in the legal profession, guiding how we recruit, retain, and advance talent at every level. We are intentional about fostering a supportive culture and inclusive workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging and has an equal opportunity to succeed. That same commitment extends beyond our walls, as we engage with the broader community through pro bono work, public interest partnerships, and initiatives aimed at promoting social justice and expanding access to the legal profession. Recent initiatives include: Pro bono partnerships benefiting low-income, underserved communities, with unlimited billable credit for associates Volunteer efforts and fundraising for a variety of causes that matter to the communities where we live and work Book scholarships for first-year law students in Southern California Longstanding participation in the Association of Corporate Counsel SoCal Summer Internship Program Leadership roles held by our attorneys in various legal and business organizations Support for mission-driven organizations and local businesses Internal and external programming, including educational events and community-building activities Giving Back Community involvement is an important part of Greenberg Glusker's culture. We believe giving back strengthens not only the communities we serve, but also the connections within our own Firm. In addition to our commitment to pro bono service, our team regularly participates in volunteer initiatives and charitable fundraising throughout the year. Recent examples include: Law Rocks Fundraiser – Greenberg Glusker’s in-house band, The Gee Gees, have participated three years in a row in the annual Law Rocks Los Angeles competition. The band has won the Judge’s Choice Award and has raised tens of thousands of dollars for local charities like Alliance for Children’s Rights and TreePeople. Starve-A-Vampire Blood Drive – In partnership with the American Red Cross, team members participate in our annual October blood drive, complete with festive decorations, refreshments, and music. Last year alone, 30 participants helped support up to 90 lives. Food From The Bar – Through creative fundraising events – including Pie-a-Partner, lip sync competitions, karaoke, casino nights, comedy shows, and magic shows – we have raised thousands of dollars for the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank. Adopt-A-Family – Every holiday season, our team comes together to provide gifts and support for families in need. Volunteer Service – From building homes with Habitat for Humanity to preparing meals at Our Big Kitchen Los Angeles, our team enjoys opportunities to serve the community together. A Culture of Appreciation At Greenberg Glusker, we profoundly subscribe to the belief that our workforce is our most valuable asset, and we pair that belief with action to ensure that our team members feel valued: Administrative Professionals Day – Each year, we recognize Administrative Professionals Day with a week of appreciation events, which have included firm-sponsored massages, catered treats, gifts, and attorneys serving breakfast to our staff. Personal & Professional Milestones – Throughout the year, we celebrate birthdays, work anniversaries, engagements, weddings, growing families, retirements, and other personal milestones through our firm newsletter and office celebrations. Years of Service Recognition – At our annual holiday party, team members receive a Greenberg Glusker lapel pin upon reaching five years with the Firm, and for every five years thereafter, a diamond is added to the pin – a meaningful tradition to honor long-term dedication and commitment. Building Community Beyond the Office Greenberg Glusker creates opportunities throughout the year for colleagues to connect outside of client work. Beyond the design of our Century City office, which features open kitchens and collaborative gathering spaces that encourage conversation, teamwork, and spontaneous connection throughout the day, examples include: Attorney Retreats & Ski Trips – Each year, our attorneys enjoy a weekend retreat in Ojai, California, as well as an annual ski trip, providing opportunities to build relationships, recharge, and connect outside the office. July 4th Family Breakfast – An annual summertime tradition where team members and their families gather for breakfast, face painting, balloon artists, crafts, and other family-friendly activities. Private Movie Screenings – Whether celebrating the release of a highly anticipated film or one our attorneys helped bring to life, we host private screenings at the AMC Century City theater, often inviting team members to bring a guest. Halloween Celebration & Office Trick-or-Treating – One of our most anticipated annual traditions, Halloween at Greenberg Glusker features festive decorations, themed lunches, costume contests, and office-wide trick-or-treating for employees' children, with candy stations hosted across all three floors. Thanksgiving Potluck – Before the holiday, team members gather to share homemade dishes while the Firm provides turkey and other favorites. Those who prefer not to cook can instead support the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank through a charitable donation, making the event a celebration of both community and giving. And Much More – Throughout the year, you'll also find escape rooms, happy hours, Office Olympics, cocktail-making classes, office mini golf, and other opportunities to relax, celebrate, and enjoy time together.

We are accepting applications to our Denver, CO; Fort Lauderdale, FL; Grand Rapids, MI; Nashville, TN; Phoenix, AZ; and Troy, MI offices. The anticipated salary range for this position is $160,000 to $240,000. Please note that a variety of factors determine compensation, including geographic location, experience, relevant degrees and certifications, and other applicable factors authorized by law. This position also qualifies for an annual merit-based bonus. Arnall Golden Gregory LLP is seeking an associate with 3–5 years of experience in healthcare regulatory and transactional matters. This position can be located in either or Atlanta, GA or Washington, D.C. office. The expected salary range for this position is $225,000 to $310,000. lateral.Position: Junior to Senior-Level Prosecution & Counseling Associates (Quantum Computing)
lateral.Offices: Boston, Massachusetts; New York, New York; Washington, D.C.
lateral.Job Description: We are seeking junior to senior-level associates with knowledge of quantum computing to join the Electrical & Computer Technologies (ECT) group of our Prosecution & Counseling department. This position can be based in our Boston, New York, or Washington, DC office. Responsibilities include: Works closely with clients and inventors at all stages of the patent process Prepares, files, and prosecutes U.S. patent applications for complex quantum computing technologies Prepare responses to office actions and make patent application secondary filing decisions that maximize the scope of protection in view of Company’s strategic goals Conducts freedom-to-operate, infringement, and patentability analyses Qualifications: A degree in Electrical Engineering Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics, or a related field of study Knowledge of Quantum computing, preferably knowledge of photonic quantum computing, quantum error correction, quantum computing architectures Graduated with a JD from an ABA-accredited law school and admitted to the USPTO Strong written and verbal communication skills, ability to collaborate and work effectively in team settings Wolf Greenfield offers comprehensive benefits focused on the overall well-being of firm employees. lateral.Position: Commercial Litigation Associate - Class Actions - Seattle
lateral.Job Description: Ballard Spahr LLP, which recently combined with Lane Powell PC, is seeking a mid-level associate to join its Class Action Litigation practice in Seattle. The ideal candidate will have 4-6 years of litigation experience, either through a law firm or clerkship. Experience working on consumer, product liability, and/or employment related class action matters is preferred. Excellent writing skills, attention to detail, and strong academic credentials are required. In this role, an Associate will join a team representing a broad array of clients in consumer and wage and hour class action matters in State and Federal Courts. This is an excellent opportunity for professional growth in managing cases, drafting pleadings and briefs, discovery, and oral advocacy in a collegial team environment of a national law firm. Active bar license in Washington, or the ability to waive in, is required. How to Apply: Ballard Spahr is a nationally recognized law firm with more than 750 lawyers across 19 offices in the United States. A career at Ballard Spahr means joining a team of talented mentors, colleagues, and friends, supported by strong leadership that actively encourages professional growth. To apply, please submit a resume, law school transcript, writing sample and cover letter (optional) through our online application system. Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. Compensation and Benefits: The salary range for this position is from $250,000 – $305,000, which reflects the Firm’s good faith and reasonable estimate of possible compensation at the time of posting. Actual pay will depend on several factors such as the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. In addition to the salary for this position, lawyers may be eligible for an incentive bonus program and/or a profit-sharing bonus program. Ballard Spahr also offers an excellent benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, health savings accounts, flexible spending accounts, short and long-term disability, a 401(k) retirement savings plan, paid time off, ten paid holidays and an employee assistance program. A detailed summary of available benefits can be found here on our Careers website. At Ballard Spahr, we believe that our skills, perspectives, and backgrounds drive innovation and excellence, while our unique culture fosters collaboration and success. Our culture of thriving together forms the cornerstone of how we deliver exceptional service and position our firm for a strong future. We welcome and encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply. Ballard Spahr is an equal opportunity employer. We offer equal consideration to all qualified applicants, regardless of race, ethnicity, religion, age, national origin, handicap or disability, citizenship, sex, pregnancy, childbirth or related medical condition, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, transgender status, sex stereotyping, genetic information, ancestry, veteran status or any other category protected by applicable law. For questions or more information, please contact Zac Ottoson, Manager of Legal Recruiting, at ottosonz@ballardspahr.com .

lateral.Position: Private Client Services Associate (Mid-Level to Senior)
lateral.Job Description: Qualifications: Associate with 5-9 years of experience with a strong interest in practicing in the Private Client Services industry. This role is a full-time in-office (non-remote, non-hybrid) position. Candidates must be licensed to practice in the State of California. A demonstrated interest in technical tax practice through coursework, prior experience, or an LL.M. program is encouraged but not required. Salary range: $265,000 – $320,000 per year For specific inquiries, please contact recruiting@greenbergglusker.com . About Greenberg Glusker's Private Client Services Department: Our PCS attorneys counsel our clients on core estate planning, privacy structures, advanced gift, estate, and generation-skipping transfer tax planning, California property tax planning, residency planning for transitory clients, whether the move is occurring domestically within the U.S. or inbound or outbound international migration, foreign trusts with U.S. assets or U.S. beneficiaries, pre- and post-liquidity event planning, post death trust and probate administration, fiduciary income tax planning, trust and estate contention, fiduciary and beneficiary litigation, charitable planning, grant making, and administration of not-for-profit organizations. Our group provides continual support for the development of its attorneys in the technical areas of the practice, industry recognition, and professional development. lateral.Offices: San Francisco, California; Silicon Valley, California
lateral.Job Description: Sheppard, a global Am Law 50 firm, is seeking a mid-level litigation associate to join our nationally recognized Private Wealth and Fiduciary Litigation Team. This position is based in our Silicon Valley office, or in San Francisco, with preference for Silicon Valley. Our team includes some of the most respected and successful trial attorneys in the nation, with expertise in disputes involving private wealth. We handle complex cases relating to trusts, decedents’ estates, conservatorships, and adult guardianships. Our attorneys represent clients in matters involving breach of fiduciary duty, fiduciary misconduct and fraud, misfeasance and malfeasance in estate administration, investment mismanagement, financial elder abuse, conservatorship matters, and will and trust contests. Our litigators have achieved major victories in jurisdictions across the U.S. and internationally, regularly winning multi-million-dollar cases. Members of our Private Wealth and Fiduciary Litigation team also have authored and influenced some of the most important legislation affecting the rights of beneficiaries and rules governing fiduciaries. Associates on our team are given a high level of responsibility early in their careers and have opportunities to gain trial experience, work on fascinating legal issues, and have direct and frequent client contact on cases that profoundly affect families and organizations. This is a great opportunity to develop business and client relationships in a specialized, niche practice. The ideal candidate will have the following qualifications: 2-4 years of litigation experience Trusts and estates litigation experience, or exposure to related issues, is preferred but not required Excellent writing, analytical, and interpersonal skills Candidates must be admitted to the California bar. Resume, law school transcript, and a writing sample are required to apply. The salary range for this position is $235,000 - $310,000. For questions about this position, please contact Isabella LeBlanc at ileblanc@sheppard.com . Req #: 2026-360

lateral.Position: Commercial Litigation & Complex Trials and Labor & Employment Associate (New Haven)
lateral.Job Description: Barclay Damon LLP, a leading law firm of approximately 300 attorneys that operates from a strategic platform of offices in Albany, Boston, Buffalo, New Haven, New York City, Rochester, Syracuse, Washington DC, and Toronto, is seeking an associate for its New Haven, Connecticut, office to be part of the firm’s Commercial Litigation & Complex Trials and Labor & Employment Practice Areas, with likely exposure to various other types of litigation. The successful candidate will have a minimum of two to three years of litigation experience, which may include clerkship experience. Experience handling all aspects of a litigation file is preferred; experience with labor and employment legal issues will also be highly regarded. Candidates must be licensed to practice in Connecticut, and a dual bar in New York State or a willingness to seek admission to practice in New York is preferred. Candidates must have superior verbal, writing, and interpersonal skills and have demonstrated abilities to work directly with clients and develop and execute service strategies. Barclay Damon is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

lateral.Position: Dallas Corporate, Commercial Transactions and Outsourcing Associate
lateral.Job Description: Winstead PC is seeking a mid-level associate (3-4 years of experience) for a position with our Corporate, Commercial Transactions and Outsourcing (CCTO) practice group in Dallas. This practice is primarily focused on the aviation industry , handling myriad of sophisticated transactions for the world's largest airlines. The ideal candidate will have experience in the following areas: Corporate Transactions: Experience with transactional work, ideally in the corporate practice group of a large firm or company. AmLaw200 experience: We are looking for someone who is familiar with the pace and expectations of sophisticated law firm work. Writing Skills: Candidates should be proficient at complex legal drafting. Aviation experience: Experience in the aviation industry would be an asset, but is not a requirement. Why Winstead? Collegial, cooperative environment where you will have the opportunity to be mentored by more experienced attorneys, as well as the opportunity to mentor more junior associates. Competitive benefits . Clear path toward your professional goals , with specific feedback and evaluation at regular intervals. Our commitment to diversity gives you the opportunity to work with colleagues who bring a wide range of perspectives to the practice of law. Support for your developing practice, in the direction you want to go, at every stage of your life. No matter your family or personal commitments, or your long-term professional goals, Winstead PC has a place for you as a valued and respected member of our team.

Katten, a global Am Law 100 firm, is seeking a Commercial Litigation Associate to join its Los Angeles office. Qualified candidates will have 2–3 years of complex commercial litigation experience at a nationally or regionally recognized law firm and be admitted to the California State Bar. Experience drafting near ready-to-file documents such as pleadings, motions, and discovery responses, the ability to manage case files and tasks, and strong research, analysis, and writing skills are required. Experience with depositions and trial preparation activities and the desire to gain meaningful stand-up courtroom experience is preferred. Our ideal candidate will thrive in a fast-paced environment, demonstrate sound judgment, and take ownership of case responsibilities. Qualified applicants should include a resume and law school transcript with their application. The estimated salary range for this role is $235,000 - $260,000. Salary determinations are made based on numerous factors, such as, but not limited to: relevant experience and work history, graduation and class year, and practice area of the selected candidate.

lateral.Position: Labor & Employment Associate (2-4 years): Denver, CO
lateral.Job Description: Holland & Hart is seeking an Associate Attorney to join the firm in its Denver location. Holland & Hart will accept applications on an ongoing basis until the position has been filled. Position Requirements Ideal candidates will have 2-4 of years of experience in traditional labor and employment experience, be strong writers, and possess excellent research and analytical skills. Preferred candidates will possess a strong academic background, have compelling law school experience (e.g., law review, law journal, etc.) and/or have judicial clerkship experience. We are seeking candidates who can take depositions, handle administrative hearings, and serve as second chair in trials. A federal clerkship is highly desired but not required. Compensation and Expectations Holland & Hart’s compensation is merit-based—you’ll be evaluated on your individual performance and achievements and on your contributions to the team’s efforts. As required by the Colorado Equal Pay Act, Holland & Hart is providing a good faith salary range for this position (if based in Colorado): $207,500 - $225,000. Our generous bonus program rewards financial contributions and hard work and associates are also eligible for fee splits. Holland & Hart expects associates to invest 1800 hours on billable matters, 75 hours of pro bono/public service work (or 50 hours of pro bono legal work), in addition to at least 25 hours dedicated to Community-building, Diversity & Inclusion Investment hours. Contributions to the life of the firm is vital to the collective success of the firm, and we encourage our lawyers to engage in ways each person finds meaningful through various committees and firm activities. Benefits Summary Holland & Hart promotes work/life balance with a robust wellness program, unlimited PTO, a reduced time program, and a sabbatical program for eligible employees and partners. Full-time employees become eligible for benefits on the date of hire, with a benefits offering that includes medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, EAP, STD, and LTD. Additionally the firm provides enhanced parental leave for both primary and non-primary caregivers as well as an automatic Off Ramp/On Ramp program before and after parental leave. The firm offers inclusive fertility and family-forming benefits. Also available are voluntary income protection benefits such as supplemental life, accident, critical illness, and hospital indemnity insurances, as well as a 401(k)-retirement plan with a company match. In addition, the firm has programs that may provide for educational assistance, a subscription service for continuing legal education programs, free or discounted legal services, and opportunities through the Holland & Hart Foundation, which is a non-profit organization dedicated to creating volunteer opportunities for lawyers, staff, families, and friends of Holland & Hart LLP. Part-time employees may have access to some of these benefits, which may be on a pro-rated basis. Application Process Please apply directly online and be prepared to submit a resume, cover letter and law school transcripts. You may address your cover letter and/or direct application questions to Anna Bartle, Recruiting Coordinator, AJBartle@hollandhart.com . No phone calls please. We are not currently accepting applications from search agencies. Please check back for updates. Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the position has been filled. About Holland & Hart Holland & Hart is known for fostering an intentional culture that prioritizes integrity and a passion for ongoing learning and collaboration. We offer sophisticated, challenging projects and diverse, innovating clients. Holland & Hart is ranked as one of Vault’s “Best Law Firms in the Mountain States.” Our core values—integrity, excellence, innovation, teamwork, our commitment to one another, our diverse workforce, our communities, and living full lives—influence all aspects of Holland & Hart’s culture. Holland & Hart attracts those who love what they do at work as much as they love what they do on the weekend. We intentionally create opportunities for attorneys to seek balance in work and in life through longstanding programs including sabbaticals, service opportunities through the Holland & Hart Foundation, team retreats, and flexible-hour, remote, and hybrid work arrangements so they can be in the moment at their job, with their families, or when pursuing personal interests. Holland & Hart is a full-service law firm with more than 500 lawyers in 14 offices. Throughout the Mountain West, from coast to coast and beyond, Holland & Hart provides clients with astute legal counsel from a vantage like no other. For more information, visit hollandhart.com . Holland & Hart is an equal opportunity employer. Explanation of Voluntary Self Identification Opportunity for EEO-1 and Surveys Holland & Hart LLP (the “Firm”) may be required by federal law to compile and file a report (referred to as an “EEO-1”) with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. Such a report would only contain aggregated data of applicants’ gender, race and/or ethnicity, and would not identify applicants by name or other personally-identifiable information. Some states in which the Firm does business may also require the collection of such information. We provide every applicant, current employee, and newly hired employee the option to voluntarily supply the requested information. Your participation in this Section is entirely voluntary and the status of your application or your potential employment will not be affected by your decision to participate or to refrain from participating in this data collection process. The firm also gathers data regarding veteran status and LGBTQ+, both of which are not required for EEO-1 reporting purposes, however, data related to LGBTQ+ data is requested as part of other surveys or questionnaires we receive. Your decision to provide the information is also entirely voluntary, and your candidacy will not be affected by your decision to participate or not.

Farella Braun + Martel's rapidly growing employment practice seeks a skilled mid-senior associate with four to seven years of California employment law experience. Employers of all sizes face complex and ever-evolving personnel challenges, and Farella's employment law practice is up to any task — from the most complex multinational organizations to smaller, highly successful enterprises. We offer world-class experience, personal attention, and pragmatic representation in contentious matters, while also providing day-to-day counseling and management training to help clients avoid them. Our emphasis is always on finding expedient resolutions that strike the right balance between business goals, costs, and reputational risks. The ideal candidate will have: hands-on experience across the full spectrum of employment litigation, including disability accommodation, discrimination, harassment, whistleblower retaliation, wage and hour class actions, and non-compete and non-solicitation agreements; a proven track record of supervising and mentoring junior associates, managing complex matters with limited oversight, and taking ownership of client relationships; experience representing employers before federal and state courts, arbitrators, administrative agencies, and appellate courts throughout California; and entrepreneurial spirit, sound judgment, and the ability to work collaboratively across all levels of the firm. Although this is a litigation-specific role, familiarity with pre-emptive counseling — helping clients assess employment law risks before they rise to the level of litigation — is a significant plus. A successful candidate will demonstrate an ability to leverage their litigation experience and leadership capabilities to resolve our clients' most pressing employment concerns in a highly interactive and collaborative team environment. The annual base compensation range for this California position is between $265,000 and $332,500. Placement within the salary range depends upon a number of factors including but not limited to years of relevant experience and professional skills required for this role. Additional compensation may include discretionary hours-based and additional bonuses, health/welfare benefits, vacation and leave time (including parental and sabbatical) and paid holidays. In-person attendance and collaboration enable us to provide excellent client service and is critical to an Associate’s professional development. This position requires working a minimum 3 days on average in the San Francisco office.

Our Practice. The Real Estate Group at Bass, Berry & Sims is a team of professionals with a national practice spanning a variety of deal teams across asset classes. Our clients include REITs, public and private companies, private equity funds, real estate development and investment firms and family offices. Nationally ranked by Chambers USA for the past 21 years, researchers found Bass, Berry & Sims’ commercial real estate practice is known for being “extremely adept at handling complicated and sensitive matters. There isn’t any legal problem that I do not trust the firm to be able to handle.” Clients say, “The Bass, Berry & Sims team provides great service from top to bottom. No matter who is assigned to the matters I am working on, I always get strong and timely help.” (from Chambers USA 2024). Join us. We are seeking highly qualified candidates with two (2) to four (4) years of experience to join our growing commercial real estate team in the Nashville office. Candidates must have sophisticated real estate transactional experience and should have the ability to work directly with clients. Specific experience in the healthcare industry or client work in the private equity space is a plus. lateral.Position: Washington, D.C. - Cybersecurity and Data Privacy Junior to Mid-Level Associate
lateral.Job Description: Skadden is seeking outstanding junior and mid-level associates (i.e., class of 2023-2019) to join its Global Cybersecurity & Data Privacy Practice and AI Practice. Candidates should have two to six years of relevant experience, which includes handling data privacy, AI, and cybersecurity matters. The ideal candidates will have experience assisting clients with: (i) AI, cybersecurity, and privacy incident preparedness and response; (ii) conducting regulatory defense investigations relating to AI, data privacy and cybersecurity issues; (iii) building legally defensible AI, data privacy, and cybersecurity programs in the US (including for NIST, CCPA, BIPA, HIPAA, WMHMDA, and other US state and federal privacy laws); (iv) conducting AI, data privacy, and cybersecurity due diligence and M&A support; and/or (v) drafting AI, privacy, and cybersecurity policies and negotiating data processing and related agreements. High level of academic achievement and solid law firm experience preferred. A strong interest in the fields of AI, data privacy and cybersecurity is desired. Work experience in the federal government or law enforcement on AI, cybersecurity, or data privacy issues, including non-legal experience, is welcome and encouraged. The starting base salary for this Washington, D.C. position is expected to be between, $260,000 to $420,000 annually. Actual salary will be determined based on skills, experience (to the extent relevant) and other job-related factors, consistent with applicable law. This position may be eligible for a discretionary year-end bonus. Skadden’s multidisciplinary Cybersecurity & Data Privacy Practice and AI Practice assist clients in navigating the rapidly evolving AI, cybersecurity, privacy and technology landscapes. Associates who join Skadden laterally participate in an enhanced mentor program, which specifically focuses on the unique needs experienced attorneys face during professional transitions. These efforts, along with our professional development and other Skadden benefits , including a hybrid work model*, offer a dynamic environment where all can shape their own career trajectories while contributing to groundbreaking legal work. We also have an extensive pro bono program that allows attorneys to devote, and receive credit for, time for myriad causes that spark their interests and matches those interests with the legal needs in the community. *Our current hybrid work model consists of working Monday through Thursday in the office. Attorneys also receive the opportunity to work remotely for specified periods throughout the year. EEO Statement Skadden is an Equal Opportunity Employer. The ideal candidate will have 4-6 years of litigation experience, either through a law firm or clerkship. Excellent writing skills, attention to detail, and strong academic credentials are required. Our Commercial Litigation and Dispute Resolution group represents a wide range of local, national and international clients in all types of complex litigation and regularly appears in local, state and federal courts, at both the trial and appellate levels. In addition to the salary for this position, lawyers may be eligible for an incentive bonus program and/or a profit-sharing bonus program. Loeb & Loeb’s Private Client (Trusts & Estates) Department seeks an Associate with at least 3 years of law firm experience to join its Los Angeles office. The ideal candidate will have knowledge and experience with high-net-worth estate and tax planning, drafting complex trust agreements, and estate and trust administration. Sheppard, Mullin, Richter & Hampton LLP is seeking a Mid-level Litigation Associate Attorney to join our San Francisco office. We are currently recruiting for an outstanding associate with at least 3-5 years of litigation experience, for a specific role defending gig economy companies in employment-adjacent personal injury cases. This role offers lots of client contact, the opportunity to negotiate directly with opposing counsel, conduct detailed fact investigations, draft and argue motions, as well as take and defend depositions. Sheppard is a global Am Law 100 full-service law firm with over 1,000 attorneys across 16 offices worldwide. The San Francisco office currently has over 100 attorneys who practice in a variety of areas including Labor & Employment, Business Litigation, Corporate Transactions, Real Estate, Entertainment, Intellectual Property, and more. Our team in San Francisco continues to outperform and as a result continues to grow. With more than 150 attorneys in the Labor & Employment group firmwide, Sheppard has one of the largest and most prestigious practices in the country. Our attorneys advise employers of all sizes—ranging from Fortune 100 companies to high tech and traditional business start-ups—in all aspects of employment advice and counseling, disputes and litigation, international employment and mobility, and union management relations. We have considerable expertise in all matters affecting the workplace including wage and hour, class and collective actions, discrimination, harassment, retaliation, wrongful termination, employment agreements, layoffs, and ERISA. The strength and depth of our practice is rooted in our ability to provide truly full-service labor and employment law counseling. The ideal candidate should excel in the following areas: Strong litigation skills Researching, writing and arguing motions Conducting complex fact investigations and analysis Taking and defending depositions Resume, cover letter, writing sample, and law school transcript are required to apply. We will not be considering candidates for any remote roles at this time. Candidates must have high grades and be admitted to and a member in good standing of the California Bar. The annual salary range for this position is $260,000 to $365,000.

lateral.Job Description: Bond, Schoeneck & King PLLC, a full-service law firm of more than 300 attorneys with 14 offices that are located across New York State, as well as in Boston, Kansas City, FL and NJ, is seeking an experienced Business Attorney with at least five years of experience to join the firm’s large and growing business department. Location(s): Syracuse & Rochester, NY Qualifications: Applicant should have a background in: private and public merger and acquisition transactions, both in structuring and financing; general corporate counseling of for profit and not-for-profit entities, including software licensing and commercial and vendor contracting; working with closely-held and family businesses; negotiating high dollar technology, commercial and vendor contracts; and business structuring and governance. Required Competencies: J.D. degree from an accredited law school; have the ability to procure, cultivate and sustain a client base while working in a multi-office, team-based environment; possess excellent organizational, time management and intrapersonal and communication skills; be admitted and in good standing with the NYS Bar. Additionally, the successful applicant will have experience managing matters independently with limited supervision. Experience in counseling higher education institutions; health care law; emerging, closely-held, or family-owned businesses; or credit unions is a plus. Why Bond? The Bond firm has been existence for 125 years and has experienced decades of consistent growth. Many of its clients have been with the firm for decades. However, the firm is always developing new clients and new areas of practice, such as the Business Department’s very successful cybersecurity and data privacy practice group. The Business Department consists of nearly 90 attorneys located across the firm’s offices who work seamlessly in a collegial, team environment. The Business Department houses all or large portions of many of the firm’s practice groups, including: mergers & acquisitions, business transactions, business restructuring, collegiate sports, higher education, cybersecurity and data privacy, employee benefits and executive compensation, intellectual property, tax, and public finance practice groups. Due to our wide array of experience and talent, we attract challenging and complex legal work that rivals or exceeds matters handled by firms in many major metropolitan areas. At Bond, nine figure deals are often handled by three or four primary corporate attorneys, giving all attorneys substantive, hands on experience and training. This allows us to control costs for clients and prepare attorneys at Bond to independently handle projects and client interactions from the earliest stages of their careers. Despite our sophisticated practice and firm size, we are able to offer a work/life balance that is not available at large metropolitan firms. Bond attorneys are active in their communities, and we encourage these efforts. A small sampling of matters that the firm recently handled is contained in the firm’s annual report, which is available here . At Bond, we believe diversity within our ranks makes us better lawyers and a stronger law firm. We proudly value our racial, ethnic, cultural, social, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, religious and other personal differences. We are committed to the promotion of greater diversity throughout our communities and the legal profession. More information is available on our website . Attorneys who join Bond laterally will experience a broad and varied client base, a stimulating and team-oriented environment, potential for growth, a high-tech infrastructure and professional programs to enhance your skills and professional development. This is a closed search. Candidate submissions from third-party search firms are not authorized at this time. All inquiries will be kept confidential. The salary range at the Associate level is $110,000 to $155,000 and represents the firm’s good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation at the time of posting. Associates may also be eligible for a performance-based annual bonus. Bond, Schoeneck & King PLLC provides all employees and applicants an equal employment opportunity in the manner required by law in all aspects of employment regardless of race, color, religion, creed, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, military status, disability, predisposing genetic characteristics, domestic violence victim status or any other status protected by local, state or federal law. We thank all applicants for their interest and will contact those candidates who are under consideration.

All new summer associate and attorney hires must be legally entitled to work in the U.S. and not now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status.

Our New York office is looking for Judicial Bankruptcy clerks available in the Fall 2026. Applicants must be completing their judicial clerkship in 2026 and admitted to the New York Bar. Patterson Belknap Webb & Tyler LLP is accepting resumes from candidates presently serving judicial clerkships. All applicants should be interested in joining our Litigation Department with start dates beginning in Fall 2026. The expected salary range for this position is $225,000 - $365,000 per year, plus competitive benefits and bonus eligibility. Associate base compensation at Patterson Belknap Webb & Tyler is typically lock-step, based on experience. All applicants must submit a resume, law school transcript, and a writing sample. Your writing sample should: Be no more than 1250 words . An excerpt from a longer work is fine, but please choose an excerpt that a reader can understand without the context of the larger piece. Be your own original work, with no editing from others . If you do not have a writing sample that meets this requirement, please choose a sample with as little external editing as possible, and include a note with your sample informing us (i) who edited the sample and (ii) the nature and extent of their edits. However, you should provide a fully unedited sample if at all possible, and we will assume you have done so unless you tell us otherwise. Demonstrate your skills as an advocate . Ideally, your sample should show us that you can be a strong and effective advocate for our clients. As a general rule, we have found that draft briefs or judicial opinions make the best samples, and legal research memos are also fine. Academic pieces, such as law review notes, tend to be less helpful. The Patterson Belknap fellowships will be awarded to candidates who matriculate to the firm as associates, and whose accomplishments and passions demonstrate a longstanding commitment to civil rights, human rights, or equal access to justice causes. If you are interested in learning more about the Patterson Belknap Fellowship, please click here . PBWT is an equal opportunity employer. If you have questions or encounter difficulties with the electronic application, please contact legalrecruiting@pbwt.com .

Young Conaway is currently accepting applications from judicial clerks to join us in our Wilmington headquarters. Young Conaway values a well-rounded applicant with diverse skills and experiences, including academic accomplishments, prior legal experience, and participation in school and community activities. Applicants must be admitted to the Delaware Bar or willing to take the Delaware Bar Exam. To apply, please upload your cover letter, resume, unofficial undergraduate and law school transcripts, and a writing sample. Should you have any questions, please contact our Attorney Recruiting Manager, Shauna Ware, at sware@ycst.com or our Legal Recruiting Coordinator, Stacey Funk, at sfunk@ycst.com.
